title.zh: 卷158 志一百三十三 邦交六 日本
title.raw: 卷158 志一百三十三 邦交六 日本

sentences.zh: 日本久通中國。

translations.literal: Japan had long communicated with China.
translations.idiomatic: Japan had maintained relations and trade with China for a long time.

sentences.zh: 明季以寇邊禁互市，清興始復故，

translations.literal: In the late Ming, because of border raiders, mutual markets were prohibited; when the Qing arose, the former practice was restored.
translations.idiomatic: During the late Ming, piratical raids on the frontier led to a ban on trade; only with the rise of the Qing was commerce resumed.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年，平南王尚可喜致書於長崎奉行，請通商舶。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kangxi, the Prince of Pingnan, Shang Kexi, sent a letter to the Nagasaki bugyō, requesting permission for merchant vessels to trade.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Kangxi, Shang Kexi, the Prince of Pingnan, wrote to the Nagasaki magistrate to request clearance for trading ships.

sentences.zh: 閩、粵商人往者益眾，雜居長崎市。

translations.literal: Merchants from Fujian and Guangdong who went there grew ever more numerous and lived mixed together in the Nagasaki market quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian and Guangdong merchants grew increasingly numerous, settling throughout the Nagasaki trading quarter.

sentences.zh: 初有船百八十艘，後由七十艘迭減至二十餘艘。

translations.literal: At first there were one hundred eighty vessels; later they were repeatedly reduced from seventy vessels down to a little more than twenty.
translations.idiomatic: At first there were 180 ships; over time the quota was cut repeatedly from 70 until only a little more than 20 remained.

sentences.zh: 貨運中國歲限八千貫，置奉行三人譏察之，榷其稅。

translations.literal: Cargo shipped to China was limited to eight thousand kan per year; three bugyō were appointed to inspect and supervise it, and duties were levied on it.
translations.idiomatic: Annual cargo to China was capped at 8,000 kan; three magistrates were posted to supervise trade and collect customs duties.

sentences.zh: 然日本方嚴通海之禁，其國人或潛來臺灣及各口貿易，事發輒罪之。

translations.literal: Yet Japan was then strictly enforcing its prohibition on overseas contact; when its own people secretly came to Taiwan and various ports to trade, upon discovery they were invariably punished.
translations.idiomatic: Japan nevertheless maintained strict maritime prohibitions; Japanese who slipped away to Taiwan or other ports to trade were punished whenever caught.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，廣東廣西總督石琳奏，日本船避風至陽江縣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, the Governor-General of Guangdong and Guangxi, Shi Lin, memorialized that a Japanese ship had taken shelter from a storm at Yangjiang County.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32 [of Kangxi], Governor-General Shi Lin of Guangdong and Guangxi reported that a Japanese vessel had sought shelter from a storm at Yangjiang.

sentences.zh: 詔資以衣食，送浙江，具舟遣歸。

translations.literal: An edict provided them with food and clothing, sent them to Zhejiang, fitted out boats, and had them sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered that they be supplied with food and clothing, conveyed to Zhejiang, and sent home on provisioned vessels.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，浙江總督李衛以日本招集內地人，教習弓矢技藝，製造戰船，慮為邊患，奏明：「密飭沿海文武營縣，及各口稅關員役，嚴行稽查，水師兵船不時哨巡，以為有備無患之計。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, the Zhejiang Governor-General Li Wei, because Japan was recruiting people from the interior, teaching them bow-and-arrow skills, and building warships, fearing a border threat, memorialized clearly: "Secretly order the civil and military officials of coastal garrisons and counties, and the staff at each customs post, to conduct strict inspections; naval warships should patrol at irregular intervals, as a policy of preparedness without anxiety."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongzheng (1728), Governor-General Li Wei of Zhejiang reported that Japan was recruiting mainland Chinese to train in archery and shipbuilding, raising fears of a frontier threat. He proposed: "Order coastal officials and customs staff to conduct rigorous inspections, and keep naval patrols active at irregular intervals, so that preparedness forestalls danger."

sentences.zh: 上覽奏，諭曰：「昔聖祖遣織造烏林達麥爾森陽為商人，往覘其國。

translations.literal: The Emperor read the memorial and instructed: "Formerly the Sacred Ancestor sent the weaving-office official Ulinta Mai'ersen, disguised as a merchant, to reconnoiter that country.
translations.idiomatic: After reading the memorial, the Emperor said: "Long ago the Kangxi Emperor sent the weaving-office official Ulinta Mai'ersen, posing as a merchant, to reconnoiter Japan.

sentences.zh: 比復命，盛言國小民巽，開洋之舉繼此而起。

translations.literal: When he returned and reported, he spoke at length of how the country was small and the people submissive; the move to open the seas arose after this.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported at length that the country was small and the people docile; yet maritime expansion followed soon after.

sentences.zh: 朕數諭閩、廣督撫留意考察。

translations.literal: I have repeatedly instructed the governors-general and governors of Fujian and Guangdong to pay attention and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: I have repeatedly told the Fujian and Guangdong governors to keep a close watch.

sentences.zh: 聞日本近與朝鮮交親，往來無間。

translations.literal: I hear that Japan has recently drawn close to Korea in friendly relations, with constant intercourse.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Japan has lately grown intimate with Korea, with constant traffic between them.

sentences.zh: 夫安內攘外之策，以固本防患為先。

translations.literal: As for the policy of pacifying the interior and repelling outsiders, strengthening the foundation and guarding against calamity comes first.
translations.idiomatic: In securing the realm within and guarding against outsiders, strengthening foundations and preventing trouble must come first.

sentences.zh: 其體朕前諭無怠。」

translations.literal: Carry out my earlier instructions without slackening."
translations.idiomatic: See that you carry out my earlier instructions without neglect."

sentences.zh: 並頒諭沿海諸省防海。

translations.literal: He also issued instructions to the coastal provinces on maritime defense.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the coastal provinces to strengthen maritime defenses.

sentences.zh: 兩廣總督孔毓珣疏請沿海練舟師、置火器、增砲臺，並自赴廈門、虎門諸口巡察。

translations.literal: The Governor-General of the Two Guangs, Kong Yuxun, memorialized requesting that along the coast naval forces be trained, firearms deployed, and batteries increased, and that he himself go to inspect the ports at Xiamen, Humen, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Kong Yuxun of the Two Guangs asked to train coastal naval forces, deploy firearms, add batteries, and personally inspect Xiamen, Humen, and other ports.

sentences.zh: 上不欲啟外人疑懼，但令飭備而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not wish to arouse suspicion and alarm among foreigners, and only ordered preparations to be made.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not wish to alarm foreign powers and ordered only that defenses be kept in readiness.

sentences.zh: 李衛復奏稱：「日本貿易不能遽絕，請於洋商中擇殷富老成者，立八人為商總，責其分處稽察，互相繩舉，庶免日久弊生之慮。」

translations.literal: Li Wei memorialized again, stating: "Japanese trade cannot be abruptly cut off; I request that from among the maritime merchants the wealthy and mature be chosen, eight men established as merchant chiefs, charged to divide supervision and inspection among themselves and mutually restrain and report one another, so as to avoid the worry that abuses will arise over time."
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei submitted again: "Trade with Japan cannot be stopped overnight. Select eight wealthy, experienced maritime merchants as trade supervisors, charge them with oversight in rotation, and let them keep one another in check, lest abuses grow over time."

sentences.zh: 報可，

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 戶部奏請頒江海關則例，定東洋商船出口貨稅律，

translations.literal: The Board of Revenue memorialized requesting the promulgation of customs regulations for river and sea ports, fixing the tax laws on export goods for Eastern Ocean merchant vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Revenue asked that maritime customs regulations be issued, setting export duties for East Asian trading ships.

sentences.zh: 上諭：「日本商人每遇風暴，漂至沿海，情殊可憫。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: "Whenever Japanese merchants encounter storms and are driven ashore along the coast, the situation is truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Japanese merchants driven ashore by storms deserve every compassion.

sentences.zh: 其令有司送乍浦，附商船歸國。」

translations.literal: Let the local officials send them to Zhapu, where they may attach themselves to merchant vessels and return to their country."
translations.idiomatic: Order local officials to send them to Zhapu to take passage home on merchant ships."

sentences.zh: 著為令。

translations.literal: This was established as a standing order.
translations.idiomatic: This was made a standing regulation.

sentences.zh: 初，日本專主鎖港，通華商而禁西洋諸國。

translations.literal: At first Japan devoted itself to closing its ports, permitting Chinese merchants while prohibiting the countries of the Western Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Japan pursued a closed-port policy, allowing Chinese trade while barring Western nations.

sentences.zh: 及明治維新，始與各國開港通商。

translations.literal: When the Meiji Restoration came, it then opened ports and trade with various countries.
translations.idiomatic: After the Meiji Restoration, Japan opened its ports to trade with foreign powers.

sentences.zh: 後以各國咸在中華互市，同治元年，長崎奉行乃遣人至上海，請設領事，理其國商稅事。

translations.literal: Later, because all countries were trading in China, in the first year of Tongzhi the Nagasaki bugyō sent men to Shanghai, requesting that a consul be established to manage its country's merchants' tax affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As other powers were trading in China, in 1862 the Nagasaki magistrate sent envoys to Shanghai to request a consul to handle Japanese merchants' customs affairs.

sentences.zh: 通商大臣薛煥不許。

translations.literal: The Minister of Trade, Xue Huan, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Trade Minister Xue Huan refused.

sentences.zh: 三年，日本商船介英領事巴夏禮以求通。

translations.literal: In the third year, a Japanese merchant vessel, through the British consul Parkes, sought to open relations.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 a Japanese merchant ship sought trade access through the British consul Harry Parkes.

sentences.zh: 七年，長崎奉行河津又致書江海關道應寶時，言其國人往來歐洲，時附西舶經行海上，或赴內地傳習學術，經營商業，皆有本國符，乞念鄰誼保護。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Nagasaki bugyō Kawazu again wrote to the Jiangha Customs intendant Ying Baoshi, stating that his country's people traveling to and from Europe often attached themselves to Western vessels passing over the sea, or went to the interior to study and pursue business, all bearing credentials from their own country, and begging that neighborly friendship be remembered and they be protected.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 the Nagasaki magistrate Kawazu wrote again to Customs Intendant Ying Baoshi: Japanese traveling to Europe often sailed on Western ships, and those who came inland to study or trade carried official papers; he asked that they be protected in the spirit of good neighborliness.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 九年，日本遣外務權大丞柳原前光齎外務卿書致總理各國事務署，略曰：「方今文化大開，交際日盛。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Japan sent the Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs Yanagiwara Sakimitsu, bearing a letter from the Foreign Minister to the Zongli Yamen of All Nations' Affairs, which stated in summary: "At present civilization is greatly opened, and intercourse daily flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 Japan sent Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs Yanagiwara Sakimitsu with a letter from the foreign minister to the Zongli Yamen, stating in part: "Civilization is now wide open and international contact grows daily.

sentences.zh: 我近與泰西十四國訂盟。

translations.literal: We have recently concluded alliances with fourteen countries of the Western Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: We have lately concluded treaties with fourteen Western powers.

sentences.zh: 鄰如貴國，宜先通情好、結和親；

translations.literal: A neighbor such as your esteemed country ought first to open cordial relations and form a bond of amity;
translations.idiomatic: With a neighbor such as your esteemed country, we ought first to restore goodwill and kinship;

sentences.zh: 而內國多故，遷延至今，信誼未修，深以為憾。

translations.literal: yet because of many troubles within our country, matters have been delayed until today, and good faith and friendship have not been cultivated—we deeply regret this.
translations.idiomatic: but domestic troubles have delayed us until now, and cordial relations remain unrenewed, to our deep regret.

sentences.zh: 茲令前光等詣臺下，豫商通信，以為他日遣使修約之地，幸取裁焉。」

translations.literal: We now send Sakimitsu and others to your excellency to discuss communication in advance, as groundwork for sending envoys to conclude a treaty on another day; we hope you will decide as you see fit."
translations.idiomatic: We now send Sakimitsu to discuss preliminary communications as groundwork for a future treaty mission; we beg your consideration."

sentences.zh: 前光至天津，三口通商大臣成林、直隸總督李鴻章達其書總署，議允通商而拒其立約。

translations.literal: Sakimitsu reached Tianjin; the Minister for the Three Ports Cheng Lin and the Governor-General of Zhili Li Hongzhang forwarded his letter to the Yamen; it was decided to permit trade but refuse a treaty.
translations.idiomatic: Sakimitsu reached Tianjin; Minister Cheng Lin and Governor-General Li Hongzhang of Zhili forwarded the letter to the Yamen, which agreed to trade but refused a treaty.

sentences.zh: 前光謁鴻章曰：「西人脅我立約，彼此相距十萬里，尚遣公使、領事遠來保其僑民。

translations.literal: Sakimitsu called on Li Hongzhang and said: "Westerners compelled us to conclude treaties; though separated by a hundred thousand li, they still send ministers and consuls from afar to protect their nationals abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Sakimitsu told Li Hongzhang: "Western powers forced us into treaties; though separated by vast distances, they still send ministers and consuls to protect their nationals.

sentences.zh: 中、日脣齒相依，商賈往還，以無約故，反託外人代理，聽其約束，喪失國權，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: China and Japan are as lip and teeth, dependent on one another; merchants come and go—yet for lack of a treaty we must instead entrust matters to foreigners as agents, submit to their constraints, and lose national authority—nothing could be worse than this.
translations.idiomatic: China and Japan are close neighbors with constant commerce; without a treaty between us, our affairs are handled by foreign intermediaries who constrain us—there is no greater loss of sovereignty.

sentences.zh: 今特使人遠輸誠意，而其來也，西人或交尼之；

translations.literal: We now specially send envoys from afar to convey our sincerity, yet in coming here Westerners may obstruct us one after another;
translations.idiomatic: We have sent envoys from afar in good faith, yet Western powers may try to obstruct us;

sentences.zh: 若不得請，是重吾恥也，前光雖死，不敢奉命。」

translations.literal: if our request is not granted, this would double our shame; though Sakimitsu should die, he dare not return with such orders."
translations.idiomatic: if we are refused, our humiliation will only deepen; I would rather die than return with such orders."

sentences.zh: 鴻章復為請於朝，下廷議。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang again petitioned the court on their behalf, and the matter was referred for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang petitioned the court again, and the matter was referred for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督曾國籓等疏言：「日本二百年來，與我無嫌。

translations.literal: The Governor-General of the Two Jiangs Zeng Guofan and others memorialized: "For two hundred years Japan has had no quarrel with us.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zeng Guofan of the Two Jiangs and others wrote: "For two centuries Japan has had no quarrel with us.

sentences.zh: 今援西國之例，詣闕陳辭，其理甚順。

translations.literal: Now, citing the precedent of Western countries, they come to the court to state their case—the reasoning is very sound.
translations.idiomatic: They now come citing Western diplomatic precedent, which is entirely reasonable.

sentences.zh: 自宜一視同仁，請與明定規約，分條詳列，不載比照泰西總例一語，致啟利益均霑之心。」

translations.literal: They should naturally be treated alike; we request that a clear treaty be made with them, with articles set forth in detail, and that no phrase such as 'in accordance with the general Western precedents' be included, lest it awaken the idea that benefits should be shared equally [with all Western powers]."
translations.idiomatic: They should be treated on equal terms; let us conclude a detailed treaty without any clause referring to general Western precedents, lest other powers demand equal treatment."

sentences.zh: 上韙其議，允前光請，命總署答書，詔鴻章豫籌通商事。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved their proposal, granted Sakimitsu's request, ordered the Yamen to reply in writing, and instructed Li Hongzhang to prepare in advance for trade matters.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved; Sakimitsu's request was granted, the Yamen was ordered to reply, and Li Hongzhang was instructed to prepare for trade negotiations.

sentences.zh: 十年，日本以大藏卿藤原宗臣為專使來聘，命授李鴻章欽差大臣，應寶時、陳欽副之，與議條款。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Japan sent the Minister of Finance Fujiwara no Tadanari as special envoy on a mission of courtesy; Li Hongzhang was appointed Imperial Commissioner, with Ying Baoshi and Chen Qin as deputies, to negotiate the articles with him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 Japan sent Finance Minister Fujiwara Tadanari as special envoy; Li Hongzhang was appointed Imperial Commissioner, with Ying Baoshi and Chen Qin as deputies, to negotiate treaty terms.

sentences.zh: 日使初請照西約辦理。

translations.literal: The Japanese envoy at first requested that matters be handled according to Western treaties.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese envoy initially asked that terms follow Western treaty models.

sentences.zh: 久之，始訂條約十八款，通商章程三十三款，互遣使臣，設領事，以上海等十五口與日本橫濱等八口通商，而禁其私入內地，微異西國。

translations.literal: After a long time, a treaty of eighteen articles and commercial regulations of thirty-three articles were finally concluded; ministers were mutually exchanged and consuls established; fifteen ports including Shanghai were opened to trade with eight Japanese ports including Yokohama, while private entry into the interior was forbidden—slightly different from Western countries.
translations.idiomatic: After prolonged negotiations, an eighteen-article treaty and thirty-three trade regulations were concluded; ministers and consuls were exchanged; fifteen Chinese ports including Shanghai were paired with eight Japanese ports including Yokohama, with private travel inland forbidden—slightly stricter than Western treaties.

sentences.zh: 諸約既成，宗臣來獻儀物，期來年換約。

translations.literal: When the treaties were completed, Tadanari came to present ceremonial gifts, with exchange of ratifications set for the following year.
translations.idiomatic: When the treaties were signed, Tadanari presented ceremonial gifts, with ratification scheduled for the following year.

sentences.zh: 十一年，日本罷宗臣官，遣柳原前光詣北洋大臣李鴻章交日本外務卿副島照會，謂來歲與歐西諸國改修條約，欲酌改所議事件，與歐西一律，豫擬條款請商。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Japan dismissed Tadanari from office and sent Yanagiwara Sakimitsu to the Beiyang Minister Li Hongzhang with a note from the Japanese Foreign Minister Soejima Taneomi, stating that the next year they would revise treaties with European and Western countries, wished to reconsider the agreed matters to bring them into line with Europe and the West, and had drafted preliminary articles for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1872 Japan removed Tadanari from office and sent Yanagiwara Sakimitsu to Beiyang Minister Li Hongzhang with a note from Foreign Minister Soejima: Japan would revise its Western treaties the next year and wished to amend the Sino-Japanese agreement accordingly, submitting draft articles for discussion.

sentences.zh: 鴻章答以去秋甫經立約，尚未互換，此時遽行改議，殊非信守。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang replied that the treaty had only just been concluded last autumn and ratifications had not yet been exchanged; to revise it abruptly at this time was quite contrary to good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang replied that the treaty had only been concluded the previous autumn and not yet ratified; to reopen negotiations now would violate good faith.

sentences.zh: 特令津海關道陳欽等與商，均俟換約後照約商辦。

translations.literal: He specially ordered the Tianjin Customs intendant Chen Qin and others to negotiate with them; all matters were to await ratification and then be handled according to the treaty.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Tianjin Customs Intendant Chen Qin to discuss matters with them, but all changes would wait until after ratification.

sentences.zh: 十二年四月，日本使臣副島種臣來京換約，遣其隨員柳原前光、繙譯官鄭永寧詣總署詢三事：一詢澳門是否中國管轄，抑由大西洋主張？

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twelfth year, the Japanese envoy Soejima Taneomi came to the capital to exchange ratifications; he sent his attendant Yanagiwara Sakimitsu and interpreter Zheng Yongning to the Yamen to inquire about three matters: first, whether Macao was under Chinese jurisdiction or claimed by the Atlantic [Portuguese]?
translations.idiomatic: In April 1873 Japanese envoy Soejima Taneomi came to Beijing to exchange ratifications and sent Yanagiwara Sakimitsu and interpreter Zheng Yongning to the Yamen with three questions: first, whether Macao was under Chinese jurisdiction or claimed by Portugal?

sentences.zh: 一詢朝鮮諸凡政令，是否由朝鮮自主，中國向不過問？

translations.literal: Second, whether all government orders in Korea were autonomously decided by Korea, and China had never intervened?
translations.idiomatic: Second, whether Korea governed itself in all matters without Chinese interference?

sentences.zh: 一詢臺灣生番戕害琉球人民，擬遣人赴生番處詰問等語。

translations.literal: Third, regarding Taiwan aborigines who had killed Ryukyuan people, and the plan to send men to the aborigine districts to make inquiry—to such effect.
translations.idiomatic: Third, regarding Taiwan aborigines who had killed Ryukyuans and Japan's plan to send envoys to question them.

sentences.zh: 王大臣等當與辯正。

translations.literal: The princes and ministers were to debate and correct them on these points.
translations.idiomatic: The Yamen ministers were to rebut these points.

sentences.zh: 尋命李鴻章為換約大臣，與之互換。

translations.literal: Soon Li Hongzhang was appointed exchange-of-ratifications commissioner and exchanged them with Soejima.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang was soon appointed to exchange ratifications with Soejima.

sentences.zh: 副島種臣並致國書，慶賀大婚及親政大典。

translations.literal: Soejima Taneomi also presented a state letter congratulating the grand wedding and the ceremony of personal rule.
translations.idiomatic: Soejima also presented a state letter congratulating the Emperor's marriage and assumption of personal rule.

sentences.zh: 時各國因請覲，報可，副島種臣亦請面遞國書，許之。

translations.literal: At that time various countries requested audience because of the ceremonies; this was approved, and Soejima Taneomi also requested to present his state letter in person—this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign envoys were then granted audiences for the ceremonies; Soejima also asked to present his letter in person, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 尋進賀儀方物，答以禮，並給璽書。

translations.literal: Soon he presented congratulatory gifts and local products; gifts were returned in courtesy, and an imperial letter under seal was also given.
translations.idiomatic: He soon presented congratulatory gifts; the court returned gifts in kind and issued an imperial letter under seal.

sentences.zh: 副島種臣照會，使事畢回國。

translations.literal: Soejima Taneomi notified that his mission was complete and he would return to his country.
translations.idiomatic: Soejima notified the court that his mission was complete and he would return home.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章以日本換約時，其上諭內僅蓋用太政官印，未用國璽，駮令換用。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang, because when Japan exchanged ratifications its imperial rescript bore only the seal of the Grand Council of State and not the national seal, rejected it and ordered that the national seal be used instead.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang objected that Japan's ratification document bore only the Grand Council seal, not the national seal, and demanded it be reissued.

sentences.zh: 繙譯官鄭永寧謂：「本國向與西洋各邦換約，均鈐用太政官印。」

translations.literal: The interpreter Zheng Yongning said: "Our country has always used the Grand Council seal when exchanging treaties with the countries of the Western Ocean."
translations.idiomatic: Interpreter Zheng Yongning said: "Our country has always used the Grand Council seal when exchanging treaties with Western powers."

sentences.zh: 鴻章謂：「見爾國副本，聲明鈐用國璽，又上海道抄送總領事井田讓等敕書，亦用國璽。」

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang said: "I have seen your country's duplicate copy, which states that the national seal is to be affixed; moreover, the Shanghai intendant forwarded copies of the imperial orders to Consul-General Ida Yuzuru and others, which also use the national seal."
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang replied: "Your duplicate copy states the national seal is required, and copies of imperial orders to Consul-General Ida forwarded by Shanghai also bear the national seal.

sentences.zh: 鄭永寧允回國換寄。

translations.literal: Zheng Yongning agreed to return home and send a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yongning agreed to return home and send a corrected copy.

sentences.zh: 時日本未設駐京公使，交涉事託俄使倭良嘎哩代辦。

translations.literal: At that time Japan had not yet established a minister resident in the capital; diplomatic affairs were entrusted to the Russian minister Yuliyan Gagarin to handle on its behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Japan had not yet posted a minister in Beijing; diplomatic affairs were handled by the Russian minister Gagarin as intermediary.

sentences.zh: 十三年三月，日本兵船至廈門，聲稱赴臺灣查辦生番。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year, Japanese warships reached Xiamen, stating that they were going to Taiwan to investigate and deal with the aborigines.
translations.idiomatic: In March 1874 Japanese warships reached Xiamen, claiming they were bound for Taiwan to deal with the aborigines.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章致書總署，謂：「各國興兵，必先有文函知會，因何起釁。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang wrote to the Yamen, stating: "When countries raise troops, they must first send written notification stating the cause of hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang wrote to the Yamen: "When nations resort to force, they must first notify the other side in writing of the grounds for hostilities.

sentences.zh: 臺灣生番一節，並未先行商辦，豈得遽爾稱兵？」

translations.literal: The matter of the Taiwan aborigines had not been discussed in advance—how could they abruptly take up arms?"
translations.idiomatic: The Taiwan aborigine affair had not been discussed beforehand—how can they suddenly resort to arms?"

sentences.zh: 既聞美人李讓禮帶領陸軍，又雇美國水師官領兵船，欲圖臺灣。

translations.literal: It was then heard that the American James R. Wasson was leading the army, and that American naval officers had been hired to command warships, intending to take Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: It was then learned that the American James R. Wasson was leading the land force and that American naval officers had been hired to command warships for an attack on Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章復致總署，謂：「此事如果屬實，不獨日本悖義失好，即美人幫助帶兵，雇商船裝載弁兵軍械，均屬違背萬國公法，且與美約相助調處之意不符。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang wrote again to the Yamen, stating: "If this is true, not only has Japan violated righteousness and broken friendship, but Americans helping to lead troops and hiring merchant vessels to load officers, soldiers, and munitions all violate the law of nations, and moreover are contrary to the American treaty's intent of mutual assistance in mediation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang wrote again: "If true, Japan has broken faith, and American assistance in leading troops and hiring merchant ships to carry arms violates international law and contradicts the U.S. treaty's pledge of mutual mediation.

sentences.zh: 應請美使遵照公法，撤回李讓禮等，嚴禁商船應雇裝載弁兵。

translations.literal: The American minister should be asked, in accordance with the law of nations, to recall Wasson and the others and strictly forbid merchant vessels from being hired to transport officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The American minister should be asked to recall Wasson and strictly forbid merchant ships from carrying troops or arms.

sentences.zh: 日本既無文函知會，僅將電信抄送上海道。

translations.literal: Japan had sent no written notification, only forwarding a telegram copy to the Shanghai intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Japan had sent no formal notification, only a telegram copy to the Shanghai intendant.

sentences.zh: 云派員往臺灣查問，難保不乘我不備，闖然直入閩省，應先派兵輪水師，往臺灣各港口盤查瞭望，另調得力陸軍數千，即用輪船載往鳳山、琅軿附近一帶，擇要屯紮，為先發計。」

translations.literal: Saying they were sending men to Taiwan to investigate, they could hardly be prevented from taking advantage of our unpreparedness and bursting straight into Fujian; gunboats and naval forces should first be sent to patrol and keep watch at the various ports of Taiwan, and several thousand effective land troops should be transferred and carried by steamers to the vicinity of Fengshan and Langqiao, encamping at key points as a preemptive measure."
translations.idiomatic: They claimed to be sending investigators to Taiwan, but might strike Fujian while we were unprepared; gunboats should patrol Taiwan's ports, and several thousand troops should be rushed by steamer to Fengshan and Langqiao to seize key positions first."

sentences.zh: 乃日本兵船忽犯臺灣番社，以兵船三路進攻，路各五六百人。

translations.literal: Yet Japanese warships suddenly attacked Taiwan aborigine villages, advancing in three columns by warship, each column five or six hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese warships then suddenly attacked Taiwan aborigine villages in three columns of five or six hundred men each.

sentences.zh: 生番驚竄，牡丹、高士佛、加芝來、竹仔各社咸被焚。

translations.literal: The aborigines fled in alarm; the villages of Mudan, Gaoshifo, Jiazhilai, Zhuzai, and others were all burned.
translations.idiomatic: The aborigines fled in panic; the villages of Mudan, Gaoshifo, Jiazhilai, Zhuzai, and others were burned.

sentences.zh: 其時尚有兵輪船泊夏門。

translations.literal: At that time gunboats were still anchored at Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Gunboats were still anchored at Xiamen at the time.

sentences.zh: 於是臺灣戒嚴，命船政大臣沈葆楨渡臺設防。

translations.literal: Thereupon Taiwan was placed under martial law, and the Minister of the Naval Yards Shen Baozhen was ordered to cross to Taiwan to establish defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan was placed under martial law, and Naval Minister Shen Baozhen was ordered to cross the strait and organize defenses.

sentences.zh: 葆楨密疏聯外交、儲利器、儲人才、通消息四事。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen memorialized in secret on four matters: linking diplomacy, storing sharp weapons, storing talented men, and communicating intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: Shen memorialized in secret on four priorities: diplomatic coordination, stockpiling arms, training personnel, and improving communications.

sentences.zh: 閩浙總督李鶴年亦陳臺灣地利，並遣水路各營分往鳳山、澎湖等處屯紮。

translations.literal: The Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang Li Henian also described Taiwan's strategic terrain and sent naval garrisons to encamp separately at Fengshan, Penghu, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Li Henian of Fujian and Zhejiang also described Taiwan's strategic terrain and dispatched naval units to garrison Fengshan, Penghu, and other points.

sentences.zh: 是月日本攻生番網索、加芝來等社，移兵脅龜仔角社，社番誓不降。

translations.literal: That month Japan attacked the aborigine villages of Wangsuo, Jiazhilai, and others, then shifted troops to coerce Guizaijiao village; the villagers swore not to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That month Japan attacked the villages of Wangsuo and Jiazhilai, then moved against Guizaijiao, whose people refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 帝命福建布政使潘霨赴臺灣會商設防。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the Fujian Provincial Administration Commissioner Pan Wei to go to Taiwan to consult on establishing defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Fujian Administration Commissioner Pan Wei to go to Taiwan to coordinate defenses.

sentences.zh: 五月，沈葆楨、潘霨率洋將日意格、斯恭塞格至臺灣，奏陳理諭、設防、開禁等事，皆報可。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Shen Baozhen and Pan Wei, leading the foreign officers Prosper Giquel and Paul de la Croix, reached Taiwan and memorialized on reasoning with the aborigines, establishing defenses, lifting prohibitions, and other matters—all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: In May Shen Baozhen and Pan Wei, with foreign advisers Giquel and de la Croix, reached Taiwan and memorialized on negotiation, defense, and lifting trade restrictions—all approved.

sentences.zh: 初八日，潘霨偕臺灣兵備道夏獻綸及洋將日意格、斯恭塞格等，乘輪船由安平出海抵琅軿。

translations.literal: On the eighth day, Pan Wei, together with the Taiwan Military Defense Intendant Xia Xianlun and the foreign officers Giquel, de la Croix, and others, took a steamer from Anping out to sea and reached Langqiao.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth Pan Wei, Taiwan Military Intendant Xia Xianlun, and foreign advisers Giquel and de la Croix sailed from Anping to Langqiao.

sentences.zh: 詣日營，晤中將西鄉從道，示以葆楨照會，略云：「生番土地隸中國者二百餘年，殺人者死，律有明條，雖生番豈能輕縱。

translations.literal: They went to the Japanese camp and met Lieutenant General Saigō Jūdō, presenting Shen Baozhen's note, which stated in summary: "Aborigine lands have been subject to China for more than two hundred years; murderers are put to death—there are clear statutes in the law; even aborigines cannot be lightly indulged.
translations.idiomatic: They called on the Japanese camp and met Lieutenant General Saigō Jūdō, presenting Shen Baozhen's note: "Aborigine lands have been under Chinese jurisdiction for over two centuries; murder is punishable by death under clear law—even aborigines cannot go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 然此中國分內應辦之事，不當轉煩他國勞師糜餉。

translations.literal: Yet this is a matter China should handle within its own jurisdiction; it ought not to trouble another country to expend troops and waste supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this is an internal matter for China; it should not require foreign troops and expense.

sentences.zh: 乃聞貴中將忽然以船載兵，由不通商之琅軿登岸。

translations.literal: Yet we hear that Your Excellency the Lieutenant General suddenly loaded troops on ships and landed at Langqiao, which is not open to trade.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we hear Your Excellency suddenly landed troops at Langqiao, a port not open to foreign trade.

sentences.zh: 臺民惶恐，謂不知開罪何端，使貴國置和約於不顧？

translations.literal: The people of Taiwan are fearful and alarmed, saying they do not know what offense was committed, causing your country to disregard the treaty?
translations.idiomatic: The people of Taiwan are alarmed, not knowing what offense prompted your country to disregard the treaty.

sentences.zh: 及觀貴中將照會閩浙總督公文，方知為牡丹社生番戕害琉球難民而起。

translations.literal: Only upon reading Your Excellency the Lieutenant General's note to the Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang did we learn that this arose because Mudan village aborigines had killed Ryukyuan refugees.
translations.idiomatic: Only upon reading Your Excellency's note to the Fujian-Zhejiang governor did we learn this arose from Mudan aborigines killing Ryukyuan refugees.

sentences.zh: 無論琉球雖弱，侭可自鳴不平。

translations.literal: Regardless, though Ryukyu is weak, it may still voice its grievance on its own.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Ryukyu is weak, it may lodge its own complaint.

sentences.zh: 即貴國專意恤鄰，亦何妨照會總理衙門商辦。

translations.literal: Even if your country is solely intent on showing sympathy to a neighbor, what harm would there be in notifying the Zongli Yamen to discuss the matter?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Japan wished only to aid a neighbor, why not notify the Zongli Yamen for consultation?

sentences.zh: 乃積累年之舊案，而不能候數日之回文，此中曲直是非，想亦難逃洞鑒。

translations.literal: Yet this is an old case accumulated over years, and you could not wait a few days for a reply—the rights and wrongs herein can hardly escape your penetrating judgment.
translations.idiomatic: This was an old case of many years' standing, yet you could not wait a few days for a reply—the rights and wrongs can hardly escape your judgment.

sentences.zh: 今牡丹社已殘毀矣，而又波及于無辜之高士佛等社。

translations.literal: Now Mudan village has already been ravaged and destroyed, yet the harm has spread to the innocent villages of Gaoshifo and others.
translations.idiomatic: Mudan has already been destroyed, yet the violence has spread to innocent villages such as Gaoshifo.

sentences.zh: 來文所稱殛其凶首者，謂何也？

translations.literal: What is meant by your document's statement that the ringleaders were executed?
translations.idiomatic: What is meant by your document's claim that the ringleaders were executed?

sentences.zh: 所稱往攻其心者，謂何也？

translations.literal: What is meant by the statement that you went to attack their heartland?
translations.idiomatic: What is meant by your claim that you attacked their stronghold?

sentences.zh: 幫辦潘布政使自上海面晤貴國柳原公使，已商允退兵，以為必非虛語。

translations.literal: Assistant Commissioner Pan, the Provincial Administration Commissioner, met in person with your country's Minister Yanagiwara in Shanghai and had already agreed on withdrawal of troops—we took this to be no empty promise.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Commissioner Pan met Minister Yanagiwara in Shanghai and obtained agreement to withdraw troops—we took that promise seriously.

sentences.zh: 乃聞貴中將仍紮營牡丹社，且有將攻卑南社之謠。

translations.literal: Yet we hear that Your Excellency the Lieutenant General is still encamped at Mudan village, and there are rumors of an attack on Beinan village.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we hear Your Excellency remains encamped at Mudan, with rumors of an attack on Beinan.

sentences.zh: 夫牡丹社戕琉球難民者也。

translations.literal: It was Mudan village that killed the Ryukyuan refugees.
translations.idiomatic: It was Mudan village that killed the Ryukyuan refugees.

sentences.zh: 卑南社救貴國難民者也。

translations.literal: Beinan village was the one that rescued your country's refugees.
translations.idiomatic: It was Beinan village that rescued your country's refugees.

sentences.zh: 以德為怨，想貴中將必不其然。

translations.literal: To repay kindness with enmity—Your Excellency the Lieutenant General surely would not do so.
translations.idiomatic: Surely Your Excellency would not repay kindness with enmity.

sentences.zh: 第貴中將知會閩浙總督公文，有佐藤利八至卑南番地亦被劫掠之語，誠恐謠傳未必無因。

translations.literal: Only, in Your Excellency the Lieutenant General's notification to the Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang, there is mention that Satō Rihachi, upon reaching Beinan aborigine territory, was also robbed and plundered—we truly fear rumors may not be without foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Your note to the Fujian-Zhejiang governor mentions that Satō Rihachi was robbed in Beinan territory; we fear there may be some truth to the rumor.

sentences.zh: 夫鳧水逃生者，有餘資可劫，天下有劫人之財，肯養其人數月不受值者耶？

translations.literal: For those who fled over water to escape death, if they had surplus wealth to be robbed, in all the world is there anyone who robs people's property yet is willing to support them for months without payment?
translations.idiomatic: Refugees fleeing by sea would hardly have wealth worth robbing—who in the world robs travelers yet feeds them for months without payment?

sentences.zh: 即謂地方官所報難民口供不足據，貴國謝函俱在，並未涉及劫掠一言。

translations.literal: Even if one says the refugee testimony reported by local officials is not reliable, your country's letters of thanks are all extant, and not one word mentions robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Even if local officials' refugee testimony is unreliable, your thank-you letters make no mention of robbery.

sentences.zh: 貴國所賞之陳安生，即卑南社生番頭目也。

translations.literal: The Chen Ansheng whom your country rewarded is precisely the headman of Beinan village aborigines.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen Ansheng your country rewarded is precisely the Beinan aborigine headman.

sentences.zh: 所賞之人即所誅之人，貴國未必有此政體。

translations.literal: The man rewarded is the man condemned—your country surely has no such form of government.
translations.idiomatic: The man you rewarded is the man you condemned—surely no government works that way.

sentences.zh: 兩國和誼，載在盟府，永矢弗諼。

translations.literal: The friendship of the two countries is recorded in the treaty archives, to be kept forever without forgetting.
translations.idiomatic: The friendship of our two countries is enshrined in treaty and must never be forgotten.

sentences.zh: 本大臣敢不開誠佈公，以效愚者之一得，惟高明裁察見覆。」

translations.literal: This minister dares not fail to speak frankly and openly, to offer what little a foolish man may contribute; I beg your lofty wisdom to examine and reply."
translations.idiomatic: I speak frankly in the hope of a wise reply.

sentences.zh: 霨復造其營，從道辭以病。

translations.literal: Pan Wei again visited their camp; Jūdō excused himself on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Wei visited the camp again; Saigō pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 霨及獻綸遂遣人傳各社番目，至者凡十五社，譯傳大意，皆求保護。

translations.literal: Pan Wei and Xia Xianlun then sent men to summon the headmen of the various villages; fifteen villages came in all; the gist was translated, and all sought protection.
translations.idiomatic: Pan and Xia summoned aborigine headmen from fifteen villages, all seeking protection.

sentences.zh: 因諭令具狀，原遵約束，不敢劫殺。

translations.literal: They were therefore instructed to submit written statements pledging to abide by regulations and not dare to rob or kill.
translations.idiomatic: They were instructed to submit written pledges to obey regulations and refrain from robbery and killing.

sentences.zh: 霨等宣示國家德意，加以犒賞。

translations.literal: Pan Wei and the others proclaimed the state's benevolent intent and gave rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Pan and his party proclaimed imperial benevolence and distributed rewards.

sentences.zh: 番目等咸求設官經理，永隸編氓。

translations.literal: The headmen all asked that officials be appointed to administer them, that they might forever be registered subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The headmen all asked for official administration so they might be permanently registered as subjects.

sentences.zh: 霨等因從道不出，將還。

translations.literal: Pan Wei and the others, because Jūdō would not come out, prepared to return.
translations.idiomatic: Pan and his party prepared to return because Saigō would not receive them.

sentences.zh: 從道復來謁，堅以生番非中國版圖為詞。

translations.literal: Jūdō came again to call on them, insisting that the aborigines were not within China's territorial map.
translations.idiomatic: Saigō called again, insisting the aborigines were not Chinese territory.

sentences.zh: 及示以臺灣府志所載生番歲輸番餉之數，與各社所具結狀，日將始婉謝。

translations.literal: When shown the Taiwan prefectural gazetteer's record of the annual aborigine tribute payments and the written pledges from each village, he at last began to yield politely.
translations.idiomatic: Shown the Taiwan gazetteer's records of aborigine tribute and the villages' pledges, he finally yielded politely.

sentences.zh: 請遣人附我輪船，一至上海，致書柳原前光，一請廈門電報本國，暫止添兵。

translations.literal: He requested that men be sent on our steamer—one to Shanghai to write to Yanagiwara Sakimitsu, one to request that Xiamen telegraph his country to halt reinforcements for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to send men on the Chinese steamer—one to Shanghai to write Yanagiwara, one to have Xiamen telegraph Japan to halt reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 霨等遂返。

translations.literal: Pan Wei and the others then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Pan and his party then returned.

sentences.zh: 初，日本逐牡丹社番踞其地。

translations.literal: At first, Japan drove out the Mudan village aborigines and occupied their land.
translations.idiomatic: Japan first drove out the Mudan aborigines and occupied their land.

sentences.zh: 旋有輪船二先後至，一逕往後山射藔港，一載兵二百、婦人十餘泊射藔港，攜食物什具農器，及花果草木各種，分植龜潭、後灣，為久居計。

translations.literal: Soon two steamers arrived in succession; one went straight to the rear mountains at Sheliao Harbor, the other carrying two hundred soldiers and more than ten women anchored at Sheliao Harbor, bringing food, utensils, farm tools, and various kinds of flowers, fruit, trees, and plants, planting them at Guitan and Houwan as a plan for long residence.
translations.idiomatic: Two steamers soon arrived: one went to Sheliao Harbor in the rear mountains; the other, carrying two hundred troops and more than ten women, anchored there with supplies, farm tools, and plants for long-term settlement at Guitan and Houwan.

sentences.zh: 窺我兵力不厚，仍肆要求。

translations.literal: Seeing that our military strength was not substantial, they still made demands at will.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing China's forces were thin, they pressed their demands.

sentences.zh: 沈葆楨請派水師提督彭楚漢率師來臺灣。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen requested that Naval Commander Peng Chuhan lead troops to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Baozhen requested that Naval Commander Peng Chuhan bring troops to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 日旋增兵駐風港。

translations.literal: Japan soon increased troops stationed at Fenggang.
translations.idiomatic: Japan soon reinforced its garrison at Fenggang.

sentences.zh: 沈葆楨急飭營將王開俊由東港進駐枋藔，以戴德一營由鳳山駐東港為後應。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen urgently ordered Camp Commander Wang Kaijun to advance from Donggang and encamp at Fangliao, with Dai Deyi's battalion from Fengshan stationed at Donggang as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Shen urgently ordered Wang Kaijun to advance from Donggang to Fangliao, with Dai Deyi's battalion at Donggang in support.

sentences.zh: 日人水野遵入豬朥索、高士佛諸社，又自後灣開道達龜山巔，其風港之營將分駐平埔為援應。

translations.literal: The Japanese Mizuno Jun entered the villages of Zhulangsuo, Gaoshifo, and others, and from Houwan opened a road reaching Guishan Peak; the Fenggang camp commanders divided forces to garrison the plains as support.
translations.idiomatic: Mizuno Jun entered villages including Zhulangsuo and Gaoshifo and opened a road from Houwan to Guishan Peak, with Fenggang detachments garrisoning the plains.

sentences.zh: 因遣其通事彭城中平至琅軿，謁委員周有基，訊中國四處布兵何意。

translations.literal: They therefore sent their interpreter Pengcheng Zhongping to Langqiao to call on Commissioner Zhou Youji and inquire why China had deployed troops in four places.
translations.idiomatic: They sent interpreter Pengcheng Zhongping to Langqiao to ask Commissioner Zhou Youji why Chinese troops were posted in four locations.

sentences.zh: 有基以巡察應之。

translations.literal: Youji replied that it was for inspection patrols.
translations.idiomatic: Youji replied that it was for inspection patrols.

sentences.zh: 葆楨照會日將，勸令回兵。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen sent a note to the Japanese commander urging withdrawal of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Baozhen notified the Japanese commander to withdraw his troops.

sentences.zh: 時李鴻章亦深慮臺地兵單。

translations.literal: At that time Li Hongzhang also deeply worried that Taiwan's forces were few.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang also worried deeply that Taiwan's forces were inadequate.

sentences.zh: 及沈葆楨請借撥洋槍隊，即奏以提督唐定奎統軍赴臺灣助防。

translations.literal: When Shen Baozhen requested the loan of foreign rifle units, he immediately memorialized that Commander Tang Dingkui should lead an army to Taiwan to assist in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen requested foreign rifle units, Li memorialized that Commander Tang Dingkui should lead troops to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 葆楨亦奏稱：「澎湖為臺、廈命脈所關，守備單弱，非大枝勁旅，仍無以壯民氣而戢戎心。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen also memorialized, stating: "Penghu is vital to the life-line of Taiwan and Xiamen; its garrison is weak and isolated; without a large strong force, there is still no means to bolster popular morale and restrain enemy ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Shen also wrote: "Penghu is vital to Taiwan and Xiamen; its garrison is too weak without a substantial force to bolster morale and deter the enemy.

sentences.zh: 請催迅速前來，庶臺、澎氣脈藉以靈通，金、廈諸防亦資鞏固。」

translations.literal: I request that they be urged to come quickly, so that the life-lines of Taiwan and Penghu may thereby be kept open, and the defenses of Jinmen and Xiamen also strengthened."
translations.idiomatic: Urge them to come quickly so Taiwan and Penghu may be secured and the defenses of Jinmen and Xiamen strengthened."

sentences.zh: 奉旨俞允。

translations.literal: The imperial edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 潘霨又偕前署鎮曾元福等赴鳳山舊城募土勇，並勵鄉團。

translations.literal: Pan Wei again, together with former acting commander Zeng Yuanfu and others, went to the old Fengshan city to recruit local braves and encourage militia.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Wei went to old Fengshan with Zeng Yuanfu to recruit local braves and encourage militia.

sentences.zh: 因親履海口之打鼓山等處，踏勘要隘，建立兵柵，以待淮軍分駐。

translations.literal: He personally went to Haikou's Dagushan and other places, surveyed strategic passes, and built stockades to await the Huai Army's divided garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He personally surveyed key positions at Dagushan near Haikou and built stockades for the Huai Army.

sentences.zh: 是月柳原前光入京先謁李鴻章，鴻章遣道員孫士達往答拜，屬以到京後勿言兵費及請覲兩事。

translations.literal: That month Yanagiwara Sakimitsu entered the capital and first called on Li Hongzhang; Hongzhang sent Circuit Intendant Sun Shida to return the visit, instructing him that after reaching the capital he should not speak of military expenses or requesting audience.
translations.idiomatic: That month Yanagiwara entered Beijing and called on Li Hongzhang, who sent Sun Shida to return the visit and told him not to raise military expenses or request audience in the capital.

sentences.zh: 日本又遣大久保利通入京。

translations.literal: Japan also sent Ōkubo Toshimichi to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Japan also sent Ōkubo Toshimichi to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 美領事畢德格復出任調停，說鴻章仍允照柳原原議三條，並加撫恤賠命。

translations.literal: American consul Bidwell again undertook mediation, persuading Hongzhang still to grant Yanagiwara's original three articles, and adding consolation payments for lives lost.
translations.idiomatic: American consul Bidwell mediated again, persuading Hongzhang to accept Yanagiwara's original three points plus compensation for lives lost.

sentences.zh: 初，日人劉穆齋在花蓮港遭風，破船失銀，稱社番盜劫。

translations.literal: At first, the Japanese Liu Muqi met with a storm at Hualien Harbor, his boat wrecked and silver lost; he claimed the village aborigines had robbed him.
translations.idiomatic: A Japanese named Liu Muqi was shipwrecked at Hualien Harbor and claimed aborigines had robbed him of silver.

sentences.zh: 沈葆楨命夏獻綸集訊其地居人及船戶，查無劫掠失銀之事。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen ordered Xia Xianlun to gather testimony from local residents and boatmen; investigation found no robbery or loss of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Shen ordered Xia Xianlun to investigate; no robbery was found.

sentences.zh: 惟日人欲從生番租地，給有洋銀，番目來益不受而止，並繳出日本前給旗物。

translations.literal: Only the Japanese wished to lease land from the aborigines and had given foreign silver; when aborigine headmen from Laiyi came they would not accept and stopped, and also surrendered the flags and goods Japan had previously given.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese had tried to lease aborigine land with silver; when Laiyi headmen came they refused and returned Japan's flags and gifts.

sentences.zh: 葆楨因奏言：「日本和約第三條，禁商民不准誘惑土人；

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen therefore memorialized, stating: "Article three of the Sino-Japanese treaty forbids merchants from seducing natives;
translations.idiomatic: Shen memorialized: "Article 3 of the treaty forbids seducing natives;

sentences.zh: 第十四條，約沿海未經指定口岸，不准駛入；

translations.literal: Article fourteen: it is agreed that along the coast, at ports not designated, entry is not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: Article 14: unauthorized coastal ports may not be entered;

sentences.zh: 第二十七條，船隻如到不准通商口岸私作買賣，准地方官查拿。

translations.literal: Article twenty-seven: if vessels go to ports where trade is not permitted and conduct private commerce, local officials may seize them.
translations.idiomatic: Article 27: vessels trading at unauthorized ports may be seized by local officials.

sentences.zh: 今臺後歧萊地方，中國所轄，並非通商口岸。

translations.literal: Now the Qilai region in rear Taiwan is under Chinese jurisdiction and is not a treaty port.
translations.idiomatic: The Qilai region in eastern Taiwan is Chinese territory, not a treaty port.

sentences.zh: 此次前赴歧萊之成富清風等，攜遊歷執照，勾引土番，均違和約。

translations.literal: Nariyuki Tomokaze and others who went to Qilai this time, carrying travel permits, seduced native tribes—all in violation of the treaty.
translations.idiomatic: Nariyuki Tomokaze and others who went to Qilai with travel permits seduced natives—all treaty violations.

sentences.zh: 現已確查歧萊各社並無竊盜銀物。

translations.literal: It has now been verified that the Qilai villages had no theft of silver goods.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation confirmed no theft occurred in Qilai villages.

sentences.zh: 其繳出旗、扇各件，當即發交蘇松太道，轉給駐滬日本領事收回，將遊歷執照追銷。

translations.literal: The surrendered flags, fans, and other items should be sent to the Suzhou-Songjiang-Shanghai intendant to be returned through the Japanese consul in Shanghai, and the travel permits revoked.
translations.idiomatic: The surrendered flags and fans should be returned via the Shanghai Japanese consul and the travel permits revoked.

sentences.zh: 其違約妄為之處，應由彼國自行查辦。

translations.literal: As for their treaty violations and reckless acts, their country should investigate on its own.
translations.idiomatic: Their treaty violations should be investigated by Japan itself.

sentences.zh: 並錄民、番供結，咨呈總署，牒其外務省，轉飭日本領事照章辦理，以弭釁端。」

translations.literal: The civilian and aborigine testimony was also recorded and forwarded to the Yamen, with a note to their Foreign Ministry to instruct the Japanese consul to handle matters according to regulations, to quell the dispute."
translations.idiomatic: Testimony was forwarded to the Yamen and Japan's Foreign Ministry to handle under regulations and settle the dispute."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 命速修安平砲臺，及籌辦鐵甲船。

translations.literal: They were ordered to speedily repair the Anping batteries and arrange ironclad ships.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered rapid repair of Anping batteries and procurement of ironclads.

sentences.zh: 續諭：「日本雖未啟兵端，然日久相持，終非了局。

translations.literal: Further instruction: "Although Japan has not yet opened hostilities, a prolonged standoff is ultimately no solution.
translations.idiomatic: Further instruction: "Though Japan has not yet opened full hostilities, prolonged stalemate cannot continue.

sentences.zh: 現淮軍續抵鳳山，羅大春業抵蘇澳、滬尾、雞籠等口，調兵扼紮。」

translations.literal: The Huai Army is now continuing to reach Fengshan; Luo Dachun has already reached Su'ao, Hunei, Jilong, and other ports; troops are being deployed to hold key points."
translations.idiomatic: Huai forces were reaching Fengshan; Luo Dachun had reached Su'ao, Hunei, Jilong, and other ports."

sentences.zh: 葆楨於是設防益嚴，日人乃謀撤兵。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen thereupon tightened defenses further, and the Japanese then planned to withdraw troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shen tightened defenses, and Japan then planned withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 而西鄉從道仍遷延不即退，欲牡丹社賠給兵費。

translations.literal: Yet Saigō Jūdō still delayed and would not withdraw immediately, demanding that Mudan village pay military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Saigō Jūdō delayed withdrawal, demanding Mudan pay military expenses.

sentences.zh: 柳原前光既至京，先遞照會有「臺灣生番為無主野蠻，本不必問之中國」之語。

translations.literal: After Yanagiwara Sakimitsu reached the capital, he first delivered a note containing the words "Taiwan aborigines are masterless savages, and China need not be consulted."
translations.idiomatic: Yanagiwara reached Beijing with a note calling Taiwan aborigines "masterless savages" whom China need not be consulted about.

sentences.zh: 先請覲見。

translations.literal: He first requested an audience.
translations.idiomatic: He first requested an audience.

sentences.zh: 總署責以：「臺灣生番系中國地，不應稱為『無主野蠻』。

translations.literal: The Yamen rebuked him: "Taiwan aborigines are Chinese territory and should not be called 'masterless savages.
translations.idiomatic: The Yamen rebuked him: "Taiwan aborigines are Chinese territory and must not be called 'masterless savages.

sentences.zh: 迭次來京，並未與中國商明，何以捏稱中國允許日本自行辦理？」

translations.literal: You have come to the capital repeatedly without consulting China—how can you falsely claim China allowed Japan to handle matters on its own?"
translations.idiomatic: You came to Beijing without consulting China—how can you claim China allowed Japan to act alone?"

sentences.zh: 柳原前光答辯。

translations.literal: Yanagiwara Sakimitsu replied in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yanagiwara replied in defense.

sentences.zh: 久之，始議定三條，給撫恤銀十萬，再給修道建房費四十萬兩，定期撤兵付銀，互換條約。

translations.literal: After a long time, three articles were finally agreed upon: consolation silver of one hundred thousand taels, plus another four hundred thousand taels for road repair and building expenses, with a fixed schedule for troop withdrawal upon payment and exchange of the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: After prolonged negotiation, three articles were agreed: 100,000 taels consolation silver, 400,000 taels for roads and buildings, scheduled withdrawal upon payment, and exchange of the agreement.

sentences.zh: 於是大久保往琅軿，命領事福島九成謁沈葆楨陳五事：一，請派人受代；

translations.literal: Thereupon Ōkubo went to Langqiao and had Consul Fukushima Kusei call on Shen Baozhen to present five matters: first, request that men be sent to receive the handover;
translations.idiomatic: Ōkubo went to Langqiao and had Consul Fukushima present five requests to Shen: first, send men to receive the handover;

sentences.zh: 一，請撤銷兩國大臣來往公文；

translations.literal: second, request that the correspondence between the two countries' ministers be withdrawn;
translations.idiomatic: second, withdraw correspondence between the two countries' ministers;

sentences.zh: 一，請被害遺骸於收埋處建碑表墓，並許日人以後登岸掃祭；

translations.literal: third, request that monuments and tombs be built where victims' remains were buried, and that Japanese be permitted to land hereafter to sweep graves;
translations.idiomatic: third, erect monuments at burial sites and permit Japanese grave visits;

sentences.zh: 一，請以後臺灣交涉事件，由中國官交廈門領事。

translations.literal: fourth, request that hereafter Taiwan affairs be handled by Chinese officials through the Xiamen consul.
translations.idiomatic: fourth, handle future Taiwan affairs through the Xiamen consul.

sentences.zh: 葆楨以撫局已成，允之。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen, since the settlement was already achieved, granted these.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, since settlement was achieved, granted these.

sentences.zh: 惟於登岸掃祭一節，覆以須有領事官鈐印執照，祭畢即歸。

translations.literal: Only regarding the grave-visiting clause, he replied that consular seals and permits were required, and they must return immediately after the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Only for grave visits he required consular permits and immediate return afterward.

sentences.zh: 遂各遣員交代。

translations.literal: Each side then sent officers to hand over affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Each side then sent officers for the handover.

sentences.zh: 事訖，西鄉從道率兵去。

translations.literal: When matters were concluded, Saigō Jūdō led his troops away.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, Saigō Jūdō withdrew his troops.

sentences.zh: 是秋，日本派使臣帶兵船往朝鮮攻毀砲臺，以朝鮮砲擊日船，特遣森有禮為駐華公使，要求總署發給護照，派人前往，又欲代遞文信。

translations.literal: That autumn, Japan sent an envoy with warships to Korea to destroy batteries, because Korea had fired on Japanese ships; Mori Arinori was specially dispatched as minister resident in China, requesting the Yamen issue passports and send men, and also wishing to forward documents on Japan's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Japan sent warships to destroy Korean batteries after Korea fired on Japanese ships; Mori Arinori came as minister to request passports and document forwarding.

sentences.zh: 總署堅拒。

translations.literal: The Yamen firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Yamen firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章謂宜由總署致書朝鮮政府，勸其以禮接待，或更遣使赴日本報聘，辨明開砲轟船原委，以釋疑怨，為息事寧人之計。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang said the Yamen should write to the Korean government advising courteous reception, or better send an envoy to Japan to explain the circumstances of firing on ships, to dispel suspicion and resentment, as a plan to settle matters peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang advised writing to Korea to receive Japan courteously or send an envoy to explain the firing incident.

sentences.zh: 總署即派辦理大臣往問朝鮮政府。

translations.literal: The Yamen then dispatched a managing minister to inquire of the Korean government.
translations.idiomatic: The Yamen dispatched a minister to inquire of Korea.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮政府頗不原與日本通商往來，而日使森有禮往謁李鴻章，則以高麗非中國屬邦為詞。

translations.literal: The Korean government was quite unwilling to trade with Japan, yet when Minister Mori called on Li Hongzhang, he spoke of Korea as not a Chinese dependency.
translations.idiomatic: Korea was unwilling to trade with Japan, yet Minister Mori told Li Hongzhang Korea was not a Chinese dependency.

sentences.zh: 因提出條件三：一，高麗以後接待日本使臣；

translations.literal: He therefore proposed three conditions: first, that Korea hereafter receive Japanese envoys;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed three conditions: first, Korea receive Japanese envoys;

sentences.zh: 一，日本或有被風船隻，代為照料；

translations.literal: second, that if Japanese ships were wind-driven ashore, care be provided on their behalf;
translations.idiomatic: second, care for Japanese ships driven ashore;

sentences.zh: 一，商船測量海礁，不要計較。

translations.literal: third, that merchant vessels surveying reefs not be challenged.
translations.idiomatic: third, merchant vessels surveying reefs not be challenged.

sentences.zh: 鴻章答以高麗系中國屬國。

translations.literal: Hongzhang replied that Korea is a Chinese dependency.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang replied that Korea is a Chinese dependency.

sentences.zh: 事既顯違條約，中國豈能不問，森使急求與高麗通好，鴻章請徐之。

translations.literal: The matter clearly violated the treaty; how could China not intervene? The Japanese minister urgently sought friendship with Korea; Hongzhang asked him to wait.
translations.idiomatic: The matter violated treaty obligations; China could not ignore it; Mori urgently sought Korean friendship and Li asked him to wait.

sentences.zh: 二年八月，始命直隸候補道許鈐身出使日本，擬設理事、副理事各員。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year, Xu Qian was at last appointed an envoy to Japan, with plans to establish chief and deputy resident commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 2, Xu Qian was appointed envoy to Japan with plans for resident commissioners.

sentences.zh: 日使森有禮詣李鴻章，謂中國商民向由日本地方官管理。

translations.literal: Minister Mori called on Li Hongzhang, stating that Chinese merchants had always been managed by Japanese local officials.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Mori told Li Hongzhang that Chinese merchants had always been managed by Japanese local officials.

sentences.zh: 中國若派領事官前往，恐日本不肯承認。

translations.literal: If China sent consular officers, he feared Japan would not recognize them.
translations.idiomatic: If China sent consuls, he feared Japan would not recognize them.

sentences.zh: 鴻章答以同治十年修好條規第八條云，兩國指定各口，彼此均可設理事官。

translations.literal: Hongzhang replied that Article eight of the treaty regulations of the tenth year of Tongzhi states that at designated ports of both countries, resident commissioners may be established.
translations.idiomatic: Li replied that Article 8 of the 1871 treaty allows resident commissioners at designated ports.

sentences.zh: 茲照約選派理事，日本何能不認？

translations.literal: Now commissioners are being appointed according to the treaty—how could Japan fail to recognize them?
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners are being appointed under treaty—how can Japan refuse?

sentences.zh: 日本自訂約後，在上海、廈門、天津設立領事，中國無不照約招待。

translations.literal: Since concluding the treaty, Japan has established consuls at Shanghai, Xiamen, and Tianjin, and China has received them all according to treaty.
translations.idiomatic: Japan has established consuls at Shanghai, Xiamen, and Tianjin, all received according to treaty.

sentences.zh: 彼此一例，何能稍有區別？

translations.literal: On both sides the same rule applies—how can there be any distinction?
translations.idiomatic: The same rule applies to both sides—how can there be distinction?

sentences.zh: 森使乃不復言。

translations.literal: Minister Mori then said no more.
translations.idiomatic: Mori said no more.

sentences.zh: 是年，日本屯兵琉球。

translations.literal: That year, Japan stationed troops in Ryukyu.
translations.idiomatic: That year Japan stationed troops in Ryukyu.

sentences.zh: 福建巡撫丁日昌以琉球距臺北雞籠，水程不過千里，請統籌全局以防窺伺，報可。

translations.literal: Fujian Governor Ding Richang, because Ryukyu was only a thousand li from Jilong north of Taiwan by sea, requested comprehensive planning against covetous designs; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Ding Richang of Fujian, noting Ryukyu lay only a thousand li from Jilong, requested comprehensive planning; approved.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，日本因內亂，來借士乃得槍子百萬，政府以十萬應之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year, because of internal disorder Japan came to borrow one million Snider bullets; the government supplied one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 3, Japan requested one million Snider rounds during internal disorder; the government supplied one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 五月，琉球國王密遣陪臣齎咨赴閩，訴日本阻貢物。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Ryukyu king secretly sent an attendant bearing a petition to Fujian, complaining that Japan was blocking tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Ryukyu king secretly sent a petition to Fujian complaining Japan blocked tribute.

sentences.zh: 閩浙總督何璟等以聞，並出使日本大臣何如璋。

translations.literal: Governor-General He Jing of Fujian and Zhejiang reported this, and also the minister to Japan He Ruzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General He Jing reported this and named Minister He Ruzhang to Japan.

sentences.zh: 如璋乃往日本外務寺島宗則商議，並照會其外務卿，延不答覆。

translations.literal: He Ruzhang then went to discuss with Japan's Foreign Ministry official Shima Munenori, and also notified the Foreign Minister; replies were long delayed.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruzhang discussed with Shima Munenori and notified the Foreign Minister; replies were long delayed.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，日人驅遣琉球官員之在日本者，令回琉球，並派內務大丞松田往琉球，廢琉球為郡縣，並令改用紀元。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, the Japanese drove Ryukyuan officials in Japan back to Ryukyu, and sent Interior Vice-Minister Matsuda to Ryukyu to abolish Ryukyu as a domain and county and order adoption of the new era name.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 5, Japan expelled Ryukyuan officials in Japan, sent Matsuda to abolish the Ryukyu kingdom, and imposed the new era.

sentences.zh: 如璋函報總署，復親往見其內務卿伊藤博文及外務卿，皆不得要領。

translations.literal: He Ruzhang reported by letter to the Yamen and personally called on the Interior Minister Itō Hirobumi and the Foreign Minister, but obtained no clear answer.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruzhang reported to the Yamen and met Itō and the Foreign Minister without clear answers.

sentences.zh: 時有美前總統格蘭忒者，遊歷來華，又將有日本之行。

translations.literal: At that time former U.S. President Grant was traveling in China and was about to visit Japan.
translations.idiomatic: Former U.S. President Grant was visiting China and about to go to Japan.

sentences.zh: 鴻章因以琉球事相託，格蘭忒慨然以調處自任。

translations.literal: Hongzhang therefore entrusted the Ryukyu affair to him; Grant readily undertook mediation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang entrusted the Ryukyu affair to Grant, who readily undertook mediation.

sentences.zh: 及至日本，以琉球各島本分三部，商擬將中部歸球立君復國，中、東兩國各設領事保護，其南部近臺灣，為中國屬地，割隸中國，北部近薩摩島，為日本屬地，割隸日本，冀可息事。

translations.literal: When he reached Japan, because the Ryukyu islands were originally divided into three parts, he proposed that the middle be returned to Ryukyu to restore the kingdom, with China and Japan each posting consuls for protection; the southern part near Taiwan, as Chinese territory, be ceded to China; the northern part near Satsuma Island, as Japanese territory, be ceded to Japan—in hope of settling the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In Japan, Grant proposed dividing Ryukyu's three parts: restore the middle kingdom with Chinese and Japanese consuls; cede the south near Taiwan to China; cede the north near Satsuma to Japan.

sentences.zh: 而日本總稱琉球為己屬國，改球為縣，系其內政。

translations.literal: But Japan in general called Ryukyu its dependency, changed Ryukyu into a prefecture, and treated it as internal administration.
translations.idiomatic: Japan claimed Ryukyu as its dependency, reorganized it as a prefecture, and treated it as a domestic matter.

sentences.zh: 格蘭忒請另派大員會商。

translations.literal: Grant requested that another high official be sent to confer.
translations.idiomatic: Grant asked that another senior official be sent to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章因達總署，請照會日本外務省，請其另派大員來華會商。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang therefore reported to the Yamen, requesting that Japan's Foreign Ministry be notified to send another high official to China for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang reported to the Yamen and asked Japan's Foreign Ministry to send a senior official to China.

sentences.zh: 而日本則欲中國另派大員前往東京，或如光緒二年在煙臺會議。

translations.literal: Japan, however, wished China to send a high official to Tokyo, or to meet as at the Yantai conference in the second year of Guangxu.
translations.idiomatic: Japan wanted China to send a high official to Tokyo, or meet as at the 1876 Yantai conference.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章執不許。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang refused.

sentences.zh: 會俄因廢約事，與中國肇釁。

translations.literal: At that time Russia, because of the abrogation of treaties, came into conflict with China.
translations.idiomatic: Russia was then in conflict with China over treaty abrogation.

sentences.zh: 詹事府左庶子張之洞奏：「俄人恃日本為後路，宜速聯絡日本。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhidong, Left Sub-Reader of the Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, memorialized: "Russians rely on Japan as a rear route; Japan should quickly be brought into alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong memorialized: "Russia relies on Japan as a rear base; China should quickly ally with Japan.

sentences.zh: 所議商務，可允者早允，但得彼國兩不相助，俄事自沮。」

translations.literal: Among commercial matters under discussion, what can be granted should be granted early, provided only that the two countries do not assist each other—then Russian affairs will naturally fail."
translations.idiomatic: Grant what can be granted in trade talks, provided the two countries do not assist each other, and Russian ambitions will fail."

sentences.zh: 政府得奏，因徇日使宍戶璣之請，以南部宮古、八重山二島歸中國，而加入內地通商照各國利益均霑之條。

translations.literal: The government received the memorial and, acceding to Minister Shiodome Ki's request, ceded the southern Miyako and Yaeyama islands to China, but added a clause on inland trade applying the most-favored-nation principle as with other countries.
translations.idiomatic: The government acceded to Minister Shiodome's request, ceding Miyako and Yaeyama to China while adding a most-favored-nation inland trade clause.

sentences.zh: 宍戶璣又以本國現與西洋各國商議增加關稅、管轄商民兩事，美國已允，請一併加入條約。

translations.literal: Shiodome Ki also stated that his country was now negotiating with Western countries to increase customs duties and jurisdiction over merchants; the United States had agreed, and he asked that these be incorporated into the treaty as well.
translations.idiomatic: Shiodome also asked to add clauses on increased customs and merchant jurisdiction, which the United States had accepted.

sentences.zh: 總署以日本既與各國商議，俟日本與各國訂定後，再彼此酌議，暫不並加入約。

translations.literal: The Yamen replied that since Japan was negotiating with various countries, after Japan concluded with them, the two sides could discuss again; for the time being these would not be added to the treaty.
translations.idiomatic: The Yamen said Japan should finish negotiations with other powers first before China would discuss adding such clauses.

sentences.zh: 已定議矣，而右庶子陳寶琛以俄事垂定，球案不宜遽結，日約不可輕許上言。

translations.literal: The agreement was already settled, yet Right Sub-Reader Chen Baochen memorialized that with Russian affairs nearly settled, the Ryukyu case should not be hurriedly concluded and the Japanese treaty lightly granted.
translations.idiomatic: Though settled, Chen Baochen argued the Ryukyu case should wait until Russian affairs were resolved.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督劉坤一、出使日本大臣黎庶昌、內閣學士黃體芳各有建議，皆不果行。

translations.literal: Governor-General Liu Kunyi of the Two Jiangs, Minister to Japan Li Shuchang, and Academician Huang Tifang each made proposals, but none were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kunyi, Li Shuchang, and Huang Tifang each proposed alternatives, but none were adopted.

sentences.zh: 八年十二月，李鴻章復與總署議球案，欲就前議中國封貢議結，仍不決。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eighth year, Li Hongzhang again discussed the Ryukyu case with the Yamen, wishing to conclude on the earlier plan of Chinese investiture and tribute; still no decision.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year 8, Li Hongzhang again discussed concluding Ryukyu on the investiture plan; still no decision.

sentences.zh: 十年九月，日本公使榎本武揚請於登州、牛莊二口運豆餅。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the tenth year, Japanese Minister Enomoto Takeaki requested permission to ship bean cake through Dengzhou and Niuzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 10, Minister Enomoto requested to ship bean cake through Dengzhou and Niuzhuang.

sentences.zh: 政府以非條約所有。

translations.literal: The government held that this was not provided for in the treaty.
translations.idiomatic: The government held this was not in the treaty.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章謂：「同治元年總署徇英使之請，暫弛豆禁，而已開竟難禁止。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang said: "In the first year of Tongzhi the Yamen, acceding to the British minister's request, temporarily relaxed the bean prohibition, and once opened it was hard to forbid.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang noted the bean prohibition had been relaxed in 1862 at Britain's request and proved hard to restore.

sentences.zh: 同治八年，滬上洋商雇用輪船徑從牛莊裝豆運往長崎，當經總署飭總稅司查禁議罰，不果。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tongzhi, Shanghai foreign merchants hired steamers to load beans directly from Niuzhuang and ship them to Nagasaki; the Yamen ordered the Inspector General of Customs to investigate, prohibit, and punish, but without success.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 Shanghai merchants shipped beans from Niuzhuang to Nagasaki despite customs efforts to stop it.

sentences.zh: 以後豆石漸多流入東洋，旋值中、日訂約，其時豆禁開已十年。

translations.literal: Thereafter beans gradually flowed more into the Eastern Ocean; soon the Sino-Japanese treaty was concluded, by which time the bean prohibition had been open for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Bean exports to Japan increased; when the Sino-Japanese treaty was signed, the prohibition had been open ten years.

sentences.zh: 日使援例為請，但允以通商別口買運，至登、牛兩處，仍堅持不許。

translations.literal: The Japanese minister cited precedent in his request, but only permission to buy and ship through other treaty ports was granted; at Dengzhou and Niuzhuang they still firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Japan cited precedent; only transit through other treaty ports was allowed, not Dengzhou or Niuzhuang.

sentences.zh: 榎使所請，僅豆餅一項。

translations.literal: What Minister Enomoto requested was only the bean-cake item.
translations.idiomatic: Enomoto requested only bean cake.

sentences.zh: 中日通商章程載明年限屆滿，兩國方可會商酌改。

translations.literal: The Sino-Japanese commercial regulations state that only when the term expires next year may both countries meet to discuss revisions.
translations.idiomatic: The commercial regulations allow revision only when the term expires.

sentences.zh: 今尚未訂改期，若婉辭以緩，至重修商辦，似無不可。

translations.literal: The term for revision has not yet been set; if politely deferred, until the commercial regulations are revised there seems no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Revision is not yet due; polite deferral seems acceptable.

sentences.zh: 如仍嘵瀆，應予通融，聲明原約其餘各款照舊信守，庶於羈縻之中，仍寓限制之義。」

translations.literal: If they still press obstinately, concession may be granted, with a statement that the other articles of the original treaty remain in force as before, so that within restraint there is still limitation."
translations.idiomatic: If they persist, limited concession may be granted while other treaty articles remain unchanged."

sentences.zh: 會朝鮮亂，日本進兵，以保護使館為名，又以中國兵槍傷日本兵為口實，十一年正月，派參議伊藤博文為全權大臣，來華議事，並遞國書，進謁李鴻章。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Korea was in turmoil; Japan sent troops in the name of protecting its legation, and also used Chinese troops wounding Japanese soldiers as a pretext; in the first month of the eleventh year they dispatched Councillor Itō Hirobumi as plenipotentiary to China to discuss affairs, presenting a state letter and calling on Li Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Korea rebelled; Japan sent troops to protect its legation and cited Chinese troops wounding Japanese soldiers; in the first month of year 11 Itō Hirobumi came as plenipotentiary with a state letter to Li Hongzhang.

sentences.zh: 初日本敕書內有「議辦前日案件，妥商善後方法」之語，李鴻章以為隱括朝案宗旨。

translations.literal: At first the Japanese imperial rescript contained the words "to discuss and settle methods for the earlier cases"; Li Hongzhang took this as implicitly covering the Korean affair.
translations.idiomatic: Japan's rescript spoke of settling "earlier cases"; Li Hongzhang took this to cover Korea.

sentences.zh: 伊藤開議要求三事：一，撤回華軍；

translations.literal: Itō opened negotiations demanding three things: first, withdrawal of Chinese troops;
translations.idiomatic: Itō demanded three things: first, withdrawal of Chinese troops;

sentences.zh: 二，議處統將；

translations.literal: second, punishment of commanding generals;
translations.idiomatic: second, punishment of commanding generals;

sentences.zh: 三，償恤難民。

translations.literal: third, compensation for victims.
translations.idiomatic: third, compensation for victims.

sentences.zh: 鴻章以撤兵一節尚可商議，議處統將、償恤難民，力爭不許。

translations.literal: Hongzhang held that withdrawal of troops could be discussed, but punishment of generals and compensation he contested and would not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Li agreed withdrawal might be discussed but refused punishment of generals and compensation.

sentences.zh: 函致總署，謂議處、償卹兩層，縱不能悉如所請，須求酌允其一。

translations.literal: He wrote to the Yamen that for punishment and compensation, even if not entirely as requested, one of the two should be granted as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Yamen that at least one of punishment or compensation should be granted.

sentences.zh: 但我軍入宮保護，名正言順，交戰亦非得已，斷無再加懲處之理。

translations.literal: But our troops entered the palace to protect it—our cause was righteous, and fighting was unavoidable; there was absolutely no grounds for further punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese troops entered the palace legitimately; further punishment was unjustified.

sentences.zh: 伊藤強請三事皆允，鴻章只允撤兵，並要同撤，伊藤亦允。
